questions.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=-5x$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier cosine series of the **even** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${a}_{n}.$

$\,{a}_{n}=$ {{field-1}}
for $n\ge 1$
questions.worked_solution:
For our Fourier cosine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=-5x$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
{a}_{n}=-\frac{10}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }x\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\, & ⇒\,v=\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =-\frac{10}{\pi }(uv\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-{\int }_{0}^{\pi }v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =-\frac{10}{\pi }(\frac{1}{n}[x\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }-\frac{1}{n}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =-\frac{10}{n\pi }((\pi \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi )-0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(0))+\frac{1}{n}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }) \\  & =-\frac{10}{n\pi }(0+\frac{1}{n}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))) \\  & =\frac{10(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi ))}{{n}^{2}\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )=(-1)^{n},$ we have

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{10(1-(-1)^{n})}{\pi {n}^{2}}.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{3})$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier cosine series of the **even** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For our Fourier cosine series, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{3})$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{[3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{3})]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(\frac{3}{2}-3) \\  & =-\frac{3}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $F(x)=3x+1$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ Select the correct missing parts in the Fourier cosine series of the **even** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of the function $F(x)$ below.

$$
f(x)∼(1+\frac{3}{2}\pi )+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-1}}\cdot {{field-2}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For our Fourier cosine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=3x+1$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(3x+1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x+1\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\, & ⇒\,v=\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & =\frac{2}{\pi }(uv\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-{\int }_{0}^{\pi }v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(\frac{1}{n}[(3x+1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }-\frac{3}{n}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{2}{n\pi }(((3\pi +1)\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))+\frac{3}{n}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }) \\  & =\frac{2}{n\pi }(0+\frac{3}{n}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))) \\  & =\frac{6(\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-1)}{{n}^{2}\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, since $\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )=(-1)^{n},$ we have

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{6((-1)^{n}-1)}{\pi {n}^{2}}.
$$

Finally, the Fourier cosine series is

$$
f(x)∼(1+\frac{3}{2}\pi )+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{6((-1)^{n}-1)}{\pi {n}^{2}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(nx).
$$

questions.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=8{x}^{2}+3$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier cosine series of the **even** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For our Fourier cosine series, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=8{x}^{2}+3$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(8{x}^{2}+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{[\frac{8{x}^{3}}{3}+3x]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(\frac{8{\pi }^{3}}{3}+3\pi )-0 \\  & =2(\frac{8{\pi }^{2}}{3}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{4})$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier cosine series of the **even** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For our Fourier cosine series, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{4})$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }{[4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{4})]}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(4\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-4) \\  & =\frac{4}{\pi }(\sqrt{2}-2).\end{aligned}
$$
